sources.hazard: Hazard maps (hackathon starter kit): five tiers of a 0 to 1 flood susceptibility score, built by the organisers from the Copernicus GLO-30 elevation model (https://doi.org/10.5270/ESA-c5d3d65) and the distance to rivers and streams mapped in OpenStreetMap (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright). Real terrain and real rivers; the reading of the score as flood hazard is a constructed proxy.
sources.exposure: Exposure file (hackathon starter kit): buildings with a location, a construction class and an insured value. Fully synthetic and randomly placed.
sources.hotspots: County flood areas (hackathon starter kit): the flood hotspots named by Nairobi County in its mapping of March 2026, geocoded by the organisers through OpenStreetMap. Real places, used to check the hazard maps.
sources.wards: Ward boundaries: Omare, B.D.A. and Omare, G.J.M. (2017), Kenya County Assembly Boundaries, digitised from the IEBC 2012 boundary maps, CC BY 4.0, as published by geoBoundaries (https://www.geoboundaries.org). Processing in web/public/geo/SOURCES.md.
sources.drainage: Waterways (rivers, streams, canals, drains and ditches) and informal settlements: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0 (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright), from the Geofabrik Kenya extract of 3 May 2025 and a Nairobi extract of 10 February 2025. Processing in web/public/geo/SOURCES.md.
sources.other: Open map layers (county and sub-county outlines, schools, health and emergency services): OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL 1.0) and geoBoundaries (CC BY 4.0). Processing in web/public/geo/SOURCES.md.
